title: What does this address tell you?
description:
Write the first step of lesson 6.05's way of working: look at the address in a crash and say what it most likely means.

```cpp
std::string diagnose(std::uint64_t address);
```

Return one of these strings:

| Return | When |
|---|---|
| `"null pointer"` | the address is below 0x10000 (the 64 KB Windows never maps) |
| `"uninitialised stack"` | the address is a fill pattern of `CC` bytes |
| `"uninitialised heap"` | a fill pattern of `CD` bytes |
| `"freed heap"` | a fill pattern of `DD` bytes |
| `"freed (Windows heap)"` | a fill pattern of `FEEEFEEE` |
| `"guard bytes"` | a fill pattern of `FD` bytes |
| `"unknown"` | anything else |

A **fill pattern** address is the pattern repeated to 64 bits (`0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC`) or to 32 bits (`0xCCCCCCCC`, as in a 32-bit program or a 32-bit field), **plus a small offset** of up to 0xFFF, because the bad pointer is usually followed by a member access: `0xDDDDDDDDDDDDDE05` is freed heap plus 0x28. Only offsets added on top count, from 0 to 0xFFF; an address below the pattern is not a match.
hints: Build the 64-bit pattern from the 32-bit one: `(pattern << 32) | pattern`. Then an address matches when it is at or above the pattern and at most 0xFFF above it.
lessonTitle: A Field Guide to Memory Bugs
